prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: a square editorial cover illustration for a remote service connection in Factory's MCP library.
Input image 1 is a style reference only. Keep its reductive woodcut and cut-paper character, subtle ink-on-paper texture, bold silhouettes and considered negative space. Do not copy its branching-path composition.
Primary request: depict connectivity as one large, tangible patch cable plugged into a matching socket. A broad chalk cable curves up from the bottom-left edge into a substantial chalk connector seated in an ochre socket in the upper-right. Two smaller parallel signal traces approach the socket from above. The physical joining of connector and socket is the focal point. It must read as a connected service even at thumbnail size.
Color palette: dense olive ground, warm chalk cable, straw ochre socket, a little dark green ink. Full-bleed composition, no surrounding frame. Coherent with the reference's small-press cover collection, not a glossy hardware render.
Canvas: square, edge-to-edge artwork. Keep the joined connector within the central three quarters of the width so a portrait crop retains it.
Constraints: no words, letters, labels, logos, symbols, checks, status lights, UI, screens, books, people, arrows, fake code, gradients or drop shadows. This is an illustration of connectivity, not a factual account status.
